## The data

This TidyTuesday dataset (May 4, 2021) comes from the Water Point Data
Exchange (WPDx), a platform that pulls together water point records
collected by governments, NGOs, and researchers. Each row is one water
point, such as a borehole, well, spring, or tap, with its location,
country, water source type, install year, and whether water was
available when it was last checked. The TidyTuesday version keeps a
subset of columns and is filtered mostly to countries in Africa, with
about 470,000 water points in total.

## Plot

```{r}
library(tidyverse)

water <- read_csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/main/data/2021/2021-05-04/water.csv")

top_countries <- water |>
  count(country_name, sort = TRUE) |>
  slice_head(n = 8) |>
  pull(country_name)

water |>
  filter(country_name %in% top_countries, !is.na(water_source)) |>
  mutate(water_source = fct_lump_n(water_source, n = 5)) |>
  ggplot(aes(y = fct_infreq(country_name), fill = water_source)) +
  geom_bar(position = "fill") +
  labs(
    x = "Share of recorded water points",
    y = NULL,
    fill = "Water source",
    title = "Water source mix in the eight countries with the most records"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```
